Started in 2010, the Colourful Heritage is the first charitable initiative in #Scotland aiming to preserve and celebrate the contributions of the early #SouthAsian and Muslim communities and migrants to #Scotland.

It has created the largest online repository of oral stories, established a dedicated archive and launched a unique exhibition showcasing the communities journey. Explore these amazing resources and be inspired by the positive contributions this community have made to Scotland having turned up with just a few pennies in their pocket and starting their working life as pedlars.

Pakistan.title: Mr Ashaque Ali - A Story of Family, Sacrifices and Hard Work
Pakistan.description:
Told in his own words, Mr Ashaque Ali begins with the story of his father, Fateh Ali's journey to Glasgow. From a pedlar to a shop owner, Fateh Ali worked very long hours to support his family. Ashaque grew up helping his father in the shop, and has learned a lot of valuable lessons since then.

Pakistan.title: Mrs Perveen Sarwar - Life in Early Lossiemouth
Pakistan.description:
Mrs Perveen Sarwar reflects on what life was like growing up in Lossiemouth, Scotland. Beginning with the story of her father, Ghulam Mohammed, and his migration to Scotland, Perveen's story tells the hard work of their family. From splitting working hours in the family shop, to watching movies in the cinema to improve their English. Watch this amazing interview to understand what life was like in the olden days in Lossiemouth.

India.title: Herstory - Sawarnjit Matharu
India.description:
Watch Sawarnjit's full interview: https://youtu.be/x0szVB4KNPU

HERSTORY, EPISODE 1: Join Colourful Heritage’s Project Officer, Saqib Razzaq for coffee and conversation with Sawarnjit Matharu. 

Coined in the 1970s, ‘Herstory’ was a term used to reclaim space for the female groundbreakers of the era left out of the history books. 

Fifty years on, Colourful Heritage presents a series of talks delving into the lives of women who have transformed the South Asian community in Scotland for the better. Breaking moulds and shattering stereotypes, juggling careers with children, family and marriage, these discussions will uncover the unique stories of pioneering women in their very own words. 

Born in India and moving to Glasgow at the age of five, Sawarnjit grew to defy the expectations of friends and family to become Scotland’s first South Asian Police Woman in 1974 when she was just seventeen years old.
